SanityOps Inspect-Lite - Batch Inspection Summary

What 100 AI-agent artifacts fail on

A machine-readable summary of 100 independent inspections across four artifact categories - System Prompts, Skills, Tool Schemas and full agent suites - measured against the SanityOps quality-design rule set. Prepared as the data body for a research write-up.

Headline

Across the corpus the dominant failure mode is the same in every single-artifact family: an artifact declares its task but not the limits of its task - input and output bounds, quantity caps, termination conditions and failure handling. Tool Schemas add a second, purely structural signature: missing additionalProperties control and missing parameter constraints.

01

Scope and corpus construction

This summary covers 100 inspection reports produced by sanityops-inspect-lite v1.0.0 over a four-category slice of a larger 200-case evaluation corpus. Each report inspects one test case - a single AI-agent artifact or a whole agent suite - against the SanityOps quality-design (QD) rule families and the embedded-code quality (QC) family, in a seven-stage flow A-G.

02

Aggregate results

2.1 Counting convention (one normalised metric)

For every test case, P0/P1/P2 are the number of FAIL verdicts at each severity, summed over all executed quality-design check families for that case - QD-P (prompt), QD-S (skill), QD-T (tool schema) and the cross-artifact families QD-PT / QD-PS / QD-ST / QD-CYC - plus the embedded-code quality family (QC). Stage-E Risk-Explicit (EX) items are excluded from P0/P1/P2 and reported separately.

Reports are not uniform in how the headline count is composed: some already include embedded-code QC, others print a QD-only count with a separate positive QC clause. The convention above is applied uniformly, so a QD-only headline with a non-zero QC clause has its QC verdicts added back. This normalisation materially affects exactly one case (TC-046; see Section 8.2).

05

Recurring patterns and notable findings

5.1 P0 is concentrated in agent-suite

552 of 825 P0 verdicts (66.9%) come from the 25 agent-suite reports, whose mean is far above the single-artifact categories (34.4 FAIL/report vs 5.2-11.9). Two mechanisms: a suite is inspected against the union of Prompt, Skill, Tool Schema and three cross-artifact families; and agent-suite reports apply an L3 severity-upgrade rule (Agent L3 leads to global P1 to P0, P2 to P1), so the same underlying gap is recorded one band higher.

5.2 One boundary-declaration failure recurs across every family

The top rules in each family are the boundary sub-rules: prompt (QD-P-2.5.x input/output bounds, 2.7.x termination/data handling), skill (QD-S-1.1 / 1.3 / 4.x resource, execution and failure-handling bounds) and tool schema (QD-T-2.1 / 2.2 / 2.3 parameter constraints). The shared failure mode is an artifact that declares its task but not the limits of its task.

5.3 Tool Schemas fail structurally, not incidentally

QD-T-1.4 (uncontrolled additionalProperties) and QD-T-2.1 (missing parameter constraints) appear in essentially every tool report, and tool-schema is the only P2-heavy category (52/129, 40.3%). This is a clean, high-recurrence, mechanical signature: schema authors overwhelmingly omit the negative-space declarations.

5.4 Embedded code is most often not self-contained

QC-0.3 (elided or truncated code fragments, 19 mentions) is the single most frequent embedded-code problem - runbook snippets inside artifacts are frequently pseudo-code and are not independently runnable.

5.5 Determinism across reused source projects

Reproducibility signal

Where the same source project appears in several cases, counts are near-identical: the claude-skills prompt cases TC-078 / 079 / 080 / 083 all report 18/1/0. Repeated inspection of comparable artifacts under the same rule set yields stable counts.

5.6 Gate-0 is a corpus boundary, not a defect rate

The 75 single-artifact cases cannot satisfy Gate-0 by construction (a lone artifact has no responsibility baseline and no Tool Schema to complete). Only agent-suite cases can pass (11/25). The 89 "Not passed" outcomes therefore measure the absence of a cross-artifact responsibility context, not a quality failure of the artifact itself.

5.7 Notable Risk-Explicit items

  • NR-S-9 - explicit credential exposure in the artifact text (4 cases, incl. a GITHUB_TOKEN example in TC-003).
  • NR-S-2 - an ignored ignoreRobotsText control (TC-194).
  • NL-A-7 - reverse-constraint removal, one at P0 (TC-033).
06

Measurement framing and limitations

6.1 Unit of count

P0/P1/P2 are FAIL-verdict counts produced by the inspector, not counts of distinct defects. A single artefact defect can yield several rule verdicts (one missing boundary triggers several sub-rules; one tool schema triggers the same rule once per tool). Counts measure the rule-level verdict surface - the right unit for rule-coverage analysis - and should not be read as a defect census.

6.2 Instrument

One framework version (SanityOps v1.0, September 2026) and one inspector version (sanityops-inspect-lite v1.0.0) produced all 100 reports; counts are not comparable across other versions.

6.3 Layout heterogeneity and parser caveats

The reports span at least two layout generations. Consequences: (a) the Section 3 rule frequencies are indicative, because batch-1 layouts omit inline severity and some counts live only in headline lines - the authoritative per-case numbers come from each report's own Executive-Summary counts; (b) two Gate-0 label sets occur (G0-1..G0-4 vs G0-3/G0-4) and only the outcome is aggregated.

6.4 No inter-model comparison

The corpus was authored with two host models (DeepSeek V4 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash) but per-report model attribution is not recorded, so no model-to-model comparison is possible. A limitation to close in a future collection pass.

6.5 Corpus scope

The 100 reports are the 25-per-category inspected slice of a 200-case corpus; they are not asserted to be a probability sample, and percentages describe this slice only.

08

Aggregation coverage and self-check

8.1 Coverage

All 100 source reports were aggregated: 25 per category, every test case appearing exactly once. Two data sources are kept distinct - the curated per-case counts used in this report (each report's own stated counts) and the mechanical FAIL-line tally used only for the Section 3 rule frequencies.

8.2 Corrections applied

C-1 - TC-046

The report's headline is QD-P only (P0 = 2, P1 = 9, P2 = 0) with a separate additive line "Embedded-code QC added 2 FAIL (QC-0.3 P1, QC-1.3 P2)". Under the Section 2.1 convention the correct value is 2/10/1 (both QC FAILs confirmed at the report's lines 71 and 74). An earlier draft held 2/9/0, inconsistent with the identical handling of TC-143 / TC-146. Totals effect: sp 171/121/4 to 171/122/5; grand total 825/565/81 to 825/566/82.

C-2 - TC-140: the EX item is NL-A-7 (reverse constraint removal), severity P2, not NR-S-4.
